market_context: After Friday's sharp technology-led selloff, U.S. index futures are rebounding before the open: reports place S&P 500 futures roughly 2% higher and Nasdaq futures roughly 3%-3.6% higher, led by an approximately 8% premarket recovery in Nvidia. The 9:45 AM ET S&P Global flash PMI release is the main scheduled intraday macro catalyst; elevated 10-year yields (4.92%) and a still-high VIX (31.49) should keep the rebound volatile.

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were reported about 2% higher ahead of the cash open following last week's severe selloff, indicating broad dip-buying rather than an isolated single-stock move. The 2.23% target gain allows for some retreat from the opening gap because the VIX remains elevated at 31.49 and the 10-year yield is 4.92%.

Nasdaq futures were reported up roughly 3%-3.6% premarket, with AI and semiconductor shares leading the recovery after QQQ fell 10.5% over the prior five sessions. QQQ should outperform SPY if the Nvidia-led rebound persists, though the target is below the strongest indicated futures move to account for intraday volatility and profit-taking.

Multiple premarket reports put Nvidia up about 8% after its 14.01% Friday drop and 22.9% five-day decline, making it the principal driver of the tech rebound. A 7.86% closing gain assumes most, but not all, of the premarket recovery holds as investors reassess the recent AI-valuation selloff.

Tesla fell 7.64% Friday and 11.4% over five days, leaving it positioned to participate in a broad high-beta and growth-stock rebound. Its target gain is more conservative than the Nasdaq-futures indication because Tesla has no company-specific catalyst in the morning news flow and remains sensitive to the elevated Treasury yield.
